final_candidates.decision_summary: Disrupts zinc coordination in the RING domain, cleanly abolishing E3 ubiquitin ligase and DNA repair activity without causing global protein unfolding.
Severely disrupts phosphopeptide recognition interface in the C-terminal BRCT domain, halting tumor suppressor signaling while maintaining fold integrity.
Perturbs essential zinc binding in the N-terminal RING domain, inactivating E3 ligase function while preserving baseline backbone structure.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations are high-confidence established loss-of-function variants.

history.rationale: Cys61 is a critical zinc-coordinating residue in the N-terminal RING finger domain. Substitution with glycine disrupts RING-mediated E3 ubiquitin ligase and DNA repair activity while preserving domain fold integrity.
C61G disrupts critical zinc coordination in the RING domain, cleanly abolishing BRCA1 ubiquitin ligase and DNA repair activity.

Met1775 resides in the C-terminal BRCT domain and is key for phosphopeptide ligand recognition. The M1775R mutation abolishes peptide binding and tumor-suppressor DNA repair function without causing global domain unfolding.
M1775R severely disrupts phosphopeptide recognition in the BRCT domain, halting tumor suppressor DNA repair signaling.
Cys39 coordinates zinc within the RING domain core. Mutating Cys39 to Tyr inactivates E3 ligase activity and homology-directed DNA repair function while retaining protein expression.
C39Y impairs RING domain zinc binding and heterodimerization, inactivating tumor suppressor function.
Cys64 is part of the C3HC4 zinc finger motif in the RING domain. C64G disrupts zinc binding necessary for ligase and repair function without globally destabilizing the protein structure.
C64G mutates a conserved zinc ligand in the RING domain, resulting in loss of function while retaining baseline structural context.

Cys24 is the first conserved cysteine in the RING zinc-binding site. Introducing a charged Arg residue abolishes zinc coordination and E3 ligase activity while maintaining basic protein scaffold viability.
C24R disrupts the first zinc-binding site of the RING domain, inactivating ligase activity.
Cys44 directly coordinates zinc in the RING domain. Replacing it with bulky Phe inactivates BRCA1-mediated ubiquitin ligase and DNA repair functionality.
C44F perturbs essential zinc site geometry in the N-terminal RING domain, causing functional loss.
